mostWorthwhile.text: Adding blood to the vessel circuit was most worthwhile: the tissue-exchange inset showed oxygen and nutrients leaving, carbon dioxide returning, and red cells staying inside. It connected the transport system to cellular work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining plasma and red blood cells was straightforward, but it felt less engaging because it was the only offered combination and its result was predictable.

surprise.text: The red blood cells making ATP from sugar despite lacking mitochondria and a nucleus was an interesting contrast with the muscle cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the sequence of only one offered combination at a time left little room for meaningful choice near the end.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how circulation connects to other body systems. The exchange inset and the red-cell contrast made the biology interesting, although I would hope for more meaningful choices.
